title: Bridged license model and scheduled upgrade guardrails pilot for Private/VPC
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: design and run a 12-week pilot for a bridged licensing model and a scheduled upgrade/rollback guardrail package targeted at early enterprise Private/VPC customers. Scope includes: (1) a blended licensing proposal combining a fixed platform license fee + usage credits for burst capacity; (2) three support tiers (Standard, Enhanced, Premier) with documented SLA and included upgrade cadence; (3) a set of contract clauses and SQQ responses covering upgrade windows, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit log retention; (4) an internal ops runbook for upgrade rollback and emergency hotfixes for Private deployments. Business rationale: customers buying Private deployments have cited unpredictable upgrade cadence, unclear entitlements for emergency fixes, and overly rigid license fees. Hypothesis: offering a bridged license that reduces first-year sticker price while providing predictable upgrade SLAs will increase conversion velocity for large pilots and shorten procurement cycles by an average of 30 days.
acceptance_criteria: Draft contract addendum for bridged license + legal signoff from GC
Three pilot customers enrolled and contracted under new terms
Support tier descriptions, SLOs and pricing published in partner portal
Ops runbook for scheduled upgrades and rollback tested in staging with runbook play-by-play
SQQ template updated with KMS/HSM, audit log, and upgrade window language and validated by Security
comments: 2025-11-12 - Kickoff: met with Sales (Jin), Legal (A. Ruiz), Security (M. Thakur). Agreed scope and pilot candidate list (Acme Health, NovaFinance, EdgeRetail).
2025-11-25 - Pricing model v0 posted to Confluence. Action: Finance to provide NPV/ARR sensitivity analysis by 2025-12-05.

2025-12-05 - Finance provided sensitivity sheet (link above). Early finding: moving 25% of first-year license into usage credits reduces sticker by ~40% but increases 12-month revenue volatility. Recommend limited-time pilot only.
2025-12-16 - Legal requested clause templates for upgrade windows and emergency patch SLAs; added to contracts PR (#462).

2026-01-08 - Security completed a preliminary SQQ review. Open concerns: HSM key custody language, double-encryption for backups, and audit log retention ranges. Security asks for explicit phrase: "customer-managed KMS recommended; Redwood supports bring-your-own-key via KMS connectors."

2026-01-18 - Ops completed a dry-run upgrade in staging using the proposed guardrails. Observed: rollback path works but requires a 7-minute manual step to flush KV caches. Logged runbook task to script cache flush for automated rollback (ENG-1873).
2026-01-27 - Sales feedback from Acme Health procurement: finance team wants an explicit cap on cumulative usage credits and a quarterly invoice option. Added to decision log.
2026-01-31 - Pilot contract sent to NovaFinance; awaiting countersignature. Next: finalize partner portal documentation and schedule post-pilot evaluation on 2026-03-15.
decision_log: 11-12-2025: Pilot will be timeboxed to 12 weeks and offered as a limited opt-in to three customers.
12-16-2025: Use blended license (fixed platform fee + usage credit bucket) rather than revenue-sharing model to keep billing simple.
01-08-2026: Support tiers finalized as Standard (business hours), Enhanced (24/7 with 4h response), Premier (dedicated CSM + 1h P1 response).

01-18-2026: Upgrade guardrails will include scheduled maintenance windows, automated pre-checks, and a documented rollback path; emergency hotfix cadence capped at two out-of-band patch windows per quarter for Premier only.
